KNOWN_PREFILLS.detail: The values themselves are right: all 16 canonical and 14 boundary writes print in full and land on their own measured rules. The FAIL is that the delivered participant guide contradicts itself about one of them and misdescribes what the participant received. participant-instructions.md line 33 says the packet wrote 'your name, date of birth, case number, street address, city, state and ZIP on the proposed order'. Its later section 'What the platform deliberately left blank' then says: 'The State line at section 1 of the order. The rule Colorado draws there is 31 points wide ... and this packet writes your city and your ZIP on either side of it. Write your state on it yourself.' In the delivered canonical bytes that line is NOT blank: reports/actual-writes.json records defendant-state drawn as 'CO' at rect x 393.93 y 380.38 w 27.25, pdftotext reads 'City: Denver State: CO Zip Code: 80202', and I counted 84 added ink pixels inside that rect in the rendered page. The family's own byte proof agrees with the bytes and against the guide: blanks-left-for-the-participant.json nearMissesRefusedByRole records 'This build narrows the threshold through the module's own option, writes the state on the form's own drawn rule'. The bullet reads as a sentence left behind by the very fix build-findings.json describes (rulesOfPage minLength narrowed from 40 to 24 so this 31.25pt rule would be seen). It is unconditional, so one of the two sentences is always wrong: false for canonical, where the state is printed, and true only for the boundary case where 'Colorado' spelled out is refused as unfittable. A participant told to hand-write a state onto a proposed order that already reads 'CO' writes over correct data on the document the judge signs. Repair is in the guide generator, not in the overlay geometry: make both sentences conditional on the recorded refusal for the fixture being described.

PROTECTED_FIELDS.detail: No ink at any protected blank, proven from the rendering rather than from the field map: pages 3 of JDF 683 and 2 of JDF 686 are pixel-identical to their pinned sources, so the petitioner signature and date, the lawyer signature line, the item 14 certificate of service and its date and recipients, and the judge-or-magistrate signature and order date all carry nothing. On the two caption pages 100 percent of added ink falls inside declared write rects, so the Division and Courtroom boxes are untouched. Recorded observation, not scored as a failure: the same court-use-only block also holds the Case Number line, and the packet does write the participant's own court-assigned case number there while refusing Division and Courtroom on the strength of the same printed 'This box is for court use only' label. I do not read that as a protected write - the case number is participant-held identifying data the clerk needs to route the filing, and omitting it would be worse - but the inconsistency in the family's own reasoning is worth the Captain seeing.

COMPONENT_SET.detail: The manifest names exactly two components and both are delivered: CC-DC-CR-072B (primary_filing, required, order 1) as packet page 1 and CC-DC-089 (fee_waiver, conditional on the participant being unable to pay the $30 fee, order 2) as packet pages 2-4. Recorded as a source obligation rather than a component miss: CC-DC-089 prints on its own face that form MDJ-008, the Notice Regarding Restricted Information under Rule 20-201.1, must accompany it unless the case is one of six restricted types, and expungement is not one of them. MDJ-008 is bound to this family by no source record, the packet does not carry it and does not stand in for it, and both delivered guides tell the participant to obtain it from the Maryland Judiciary. That is the honest treatment of a companion the manifest does not name.

KNOWN_PREFILLS.detail: The 38 values themselves are correct, complete and inside their boxes on both fixtures. The FAIL is that the delivered records and the delivered guide state, three times over, that the packet wrote nothing on the court's order page while it wrote five things there. production-field-map.json refuses 18 fields on packet page 4 (CC-DC-089 page 3) and gives every one of them the same reason: 'page 3 of this form is the court's order on the request and every field on it belongs to the court'. build-findings.json says 'Page 3 of CC-DC-089 is the court's order on the request. Every field on it is refused as court-owned.' participant-instructions.md tells the participant, under 'What is deliberately left blank': 'Page 3 of CC-DC-089 is the court's order and every line on it belongs to the court.' In the delivered bytes that page carries five writes from the same field map: the DISTRICT COURT OF MARYLAND caption box is TICKED, and Court's City/County, Case No., Petitioner/Plaintiff and Respondent/Defendant are all printed. I read them off the rendered page 4 and counted their ink. The same refusals array contradicts itself in place - its first page-4 entry refuses the CIRCUIT COURT box with the reason 'the packet states the other member of this select-one', which is the tick the blanket sentence says does not exist. This is the participant-facing consequence and it is why it is a FAIL rather than a note: the caption on a proposed order names the court that will sign it and the case it will be signed in, and the packet tells the person filing that nothing on that page is theirs to check. Repair is in the copy and the refusal basis, not in the geometry: the caption is correctly filled and should be described as filled.

PROTECTED_FIELDS.detail: Nothing is signed, dated or decided for anyone. The order's 'submitted by (Name of party)' blank is also left empty even though the packet holds that name, which is the conservative direction. The five caption writes on that same page are scored under KNOWN_PREFILLS above rather than counted here, because the field map does not classify them as protected - it writes them.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.detail: This is the repaired obligation and it now holds, tested against the bytes rather than taken from the repair report. Stroke-only flattened appearances: 6 per fixture, down from the 56 VF20 scored, and each of the 6 is byte-identical to an /AP /N on-state stream in the pinned source and placed at that widget's own /Rect - the source's own X, not a synthesized square. The whole-page test is the one that would have caught the 50: differencing every delivered page against its pinned source at 130 dpi leaves ZERO added pixels outside the declared write rects on all four canonical and all four boundary pages, where each of the 50 squares would have been added ink at a rect no write declares. No value is clipped and none overlaps printed text, on either fixture, including the boundary fixture's long name, 16-character case number and two-line incident description.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: All three of MD.memo.json's selfHelpStopConditions for this track now print verbatim in participant-instructions.md, including the one VF20's superseded row found missing: 'The State's Attorney objects.' The guide goes further and explains that this condition arrives after filing and that the participant will not be the one who starts it, quoting rules.notice verbatim - 'The court serves the State's Attorney; 30-day objection period.' Four route boundaries are then stated separately and correctly labelled as route boundaries rather than record conditions.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: The memo's destination is the Clerk of the District Court or circuit court that heard the case, and its filing rule is 'File with the clerk of the court that heard the case, on CC-DC-CR-072B with the pardon checkbox.' filing-instructions.md says 'File with the clerk of the court shown in the caption - the court where the conviction was entered - unless the case was transferred or appealed, in which case the form tells you which court takes the petition', which carries the rule and the form's own exception. Items 4 and 5, which the form says decide the court, are correctly left to the participant and are called out as the two answers that decide where the petition goes.

SERVICE.detail: The record's service rule is 'The court serves.' and its notice rule is 'The court serves the State's Attorney; 30-day objection period.' The packet asks the participant to serve nobody, invents no certificate of service, and states the notice rule verbatim. filing-instructions.md adds the petition's own printed victim notice - that a victim may offer objections or additional information and that the court may act as soon as thirty days after the petition is served - which I confirmed is printed on the source binary.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.detail: All seven of the manifest's requiredBeforeFiling items are carried. Two print verbatim ('$30 (CC-DC-CR-072B).' and 'Request for Waiver of Prepaid Costs, CC-DC-089.'); the other five are carried in substance without loss - the signed gubernatorial pardon with its source and the instruction to check the pardon date before signing, the case-number check ('Check the caption, the case number, the arrest date, the arresting agency, the incident description, the offence and the conviction date against your own case record'), the signature and affirmation block, and the affirmation under penalties of perjury, which the guide states twice. Separately all 34 required-before-filing form blanks are disclosed with their printed labels. One recorded gap, not scored as a failure: the record names the free source for the case-number check, 'Maryland Judiciary Case Search', and neither delivered guide names it; the participant is told to check against 'your own case record' instead.

ARTIFACTS.detail: Both artifacts recomputed from the committed bytes: canonical 2bd8059f5970eab1ee8bb677e8006cd1a8557eba96b074b2c3eeea0d959172eb at 1,167,389 bytes and boundary a06f4ddabe754147bb8f2036d92583d5757d560aacbdd04b9deda6e55c68e3b4 at 1,167,835 bytes, 4 pages each. These are FIX01's post-repair digests, not the pre-repair ones it records as previous (cca0c00e... and c2268041...), so the bytes I read are the repaired bytes. The RASTER_PASS in product-wiring.json binds boundToCanonicalSha256 2bd8059f..., the same digest, so the admitted raster covers these bytes and not the failed ones.

PAGE_ORDER.detail: Four pages in manifest order: CC-DC-CR-072B page 1 as packet page 1, then CC-DC-089 pages 1, 2 and 3 as packet pages 2, 3 and 4. Proven page by page rather than read off the page manifest - each delivered page differences cleanly against the source page it claims, which no reordering would survive - and the order page lands last, as CC-DC-089 prints it.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.detail: Every selection the packet makes is defensible on its face, and half of them are hidden from the person who signs. The packet ticks four controls: (1) item 3's pardon ground, with the pardon date written beside it - disclosed in its own section of the guide, with the warning to check the date against the pardon document; (2) CC-DC-089's 'I request a waiver of the prepaid costs' - disclosed in one sentence; (3) the DISTRICT COURT OF MARYLAND caption box, on the petition and on both CC-DC-089 widgets, on the field map's basis 'the court of conviction held by this fixture is a District Court location'; and (4) item 1's 'I was arrested', on the basis 'the held case fact is an arrest rather than a summons or a citation'. Selections 3 and 4 appear NOWHERE in participant-instructions.md or filing-instructions.md, and the field map's own routeSelectionsMade array lists only selections 1 and 2. Item 1 is the one that matters: the form prints '(Check one of the following boxes) On or about ___, I was [ ] arrested, [ ] served with a summons, [ ] or served with a citation', the packet answers that select-one from an inference (factId null, routeDetermined false), and the petition is affirmed under the penalties of perjury. The word 'arrest' reaches the participant only inside 'check the arrest date ... against your own case record'; nothing tells them the packet chose arrested over summons or citation. Actionable repair: list all four in routeSelectionsMade and disclose selections 3 and 4 to the participant in the same terms the other two already get. Correctly NOT ticked: the other seven grounds of item 3, which the form makes a check-all-that-apply and which the packet carries as genuine participant elections with the form's own words beside each; and items 4 and 5, the transfer and appeal questions that decide the court.

REPEATING_ROWS.detail: The packet writes no repeating row. CC-DC-089's three schedules - item 3 income by source, item 4 property, item 5 debts - are the only row tables, every row is blank on both fixtures, and each line is disclosed to the participant with what it asks for. No row states part of a fact, so no row index can disagree with the label printed beside it.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: The contradiction VF20's superseded row found is gone. MD.memo.json rules.fees reads '$30 (CC-DC-CR-072B).' and rules.feeWaiver reads 'Request for Waiver of Prepaid Costs, CC-DC-089.', and both delivered guides now quote both verbatim and say '$30, keyed to this form'. The packet is candid about what the figure rests on: the two source binaries print no amount at all - the petition's only fee wording is 'Filing Fees Are Not Refundable' across the top of page 1, which I confirmed on the binary - so the guide states that the form is not evidence that the figure is current and tells the participant to confirm it with the clerk. The waiver route is not merely named: CC-DC-089 is delivered, its request box is ticked, its affidavit is left entirely to the participant because the platform holds no income, property or debt fact, and the guide tells a participant who does not need a waiver to leave the form out of what they file.
